Employee Orientation · Dungeon Operations

Rules Summary

Dungeon, Inc. is a fast, fiction-first fantasy roleplaying game about monsters employed to solve client issues — usually by exterminating adventurers — for a corporate dungeon.

⚔

The Core Loop

Describe what your monster does in the fiction. When the outcome is risky, the GM calls for a check. Roll a d20 equal to or under the relevant stat: Strength, Intelligence, Wisdom, Dexterity, Constitution, or Charisma. A 1 is a critical success; a 20 is a fumble.

Traits Change The Odds

Each character has a short trait describing their species, profession, or personality. If it helps, roll two dice and keep the better result (the lower number). If it hinders, roll two and keep the worse result.

Risk Dice

Resources and threats use a risk die, from Δ4 through Δ12. Roll it when the resource is tested: on a 1–3, step it down one size — Δ12 → Δ10 → Δ8 → Δ6 → Δ4 → Δ0. At Δ0, a resource is depleted or the threat comes to pass.

Fast, One-Roll Combat

  • No initiative: the GM follows the fiction and asks what each player does in the logical order.
  • Each character rolls once per round under the stat that fits their action.
  • On a success, the action works and the character avoids incoming attacks. On a failure, the action fails and incoming attacks hit.
  • Armor is a risk die rolled the first time it protects you in a combat scene; its result absorbs damage before hit points. Armor at Δ0 is broken.

When Things Go Wrong

At 0 hit points, a character falls unconscious and will die in about ten minutes. An ally can make a Constitution check before then; success restores 1 HP, but the character gains a lasting negative trait related to the injury.

Specialists, Martial Training & Magic

Specialists have a talent — anything from a clever magical pet to melting into shadows — and roll its Δ4 to see whether it can be used again today. Martial characters use better weapons and armor and roll stronger hit-point dice. Magical characters create spells with the GM; casting costs hit points before the spell check, so magic is powerful but never free.

The Concept

You are low-rank employees of a huge dungeon corporation. The party is made up of monsters with a job, a map, a client-facing brief, and a dangerous workplace. The mission may look like killing adventurers, but surviving the hazards, satisfying management, and getting home with your employment intact are the real adventure.

This summary is adapted from the Dungeon, Inc. Quickstart Guide. It is an orientation, not a replacement for the full quickstart.
